source.title: Algebra 1
source.subtitle: From the arithmetic it stands on to quadratic equations

f_primes_lcm.description: Uses the product of the numbers as the least common multiple even when a smaller common multiple exists.
Confuses the least common multiple with the greatest common factor.

f_order_ops.description: Works strictly left to right, adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing.
Squares the negative sign: treats -3^2 as 9.
Multiplies the base by the exponent: 3^2 = 6.

f_like_terms.description: Treats x as having coefficient 0, e.g. 4x + x = 4x.

f_translate.description: Reverses the order for 'less than' or 'subtracted from': '5 less than x' written as 5 - x.
Confuses sum and product words, e.g. 'the product of 3 and x' written as 3 + x.

f_int_add.description: Adding integers with different signs, keeps the sign of the first number instead of the one with the larger absolute value.
Subtracting a negative as if it were subtracting a positive: 5 - (-3) = 2.
Treats absolute value as 'change the sign': |-4| = -4 or |3| = -3.

f_int_mul.description: Gives a negative product (or quotient) for two negative numbers.
Applies the multiplication sign rule to addition: -3 + -5 = 8.

f_int_eval.description: Substitutes a negative number without parentheses, so x^2 at x = -3 becomes -3^2 = -9.
Evaluates the substituted expression in the wrong order of operations.

f_frac_mul.description: Cancels across a sum or difference instead of across factors.
When dividing fractions, inverts the first fraction instead of the second.
Leaves a common factor in the numerator and denominator.

f_frac_add.description: Changes a denominator to the common denominator without scaling the numerator.
Uses a common denominator that is not a multiple of both denominators.

f_frac_bar.description: Ignores that a fraction bar groups the whole numerator and the whole denominator.
Simplifies a complex fraction by dividing the wrong way (inverts the numerator instead of the denominator).

f_decimals.description: Lines up digits from the right instead of lining up decimal points when adding or subtracting.
Places the decimal point in a product by lining up rather than counting decimal places.

f_percent.description: Moves the decimal point the wrong way converting between percent and decimal: 0.3 = 3%.
Writes a percent as a fraction over 10 instead of over 100.

f_sqrt.description: Halves the number instead of taking the square root: sqrt(16) = 8.
Treats the square root of a negative number as a real number.

f_distributive.description: Distributes to only the first term: 2(x + 3) = 2x + 3.
Does not distribute a minus sign to every term: -(x - 4) = -x - 4.

lin_one_step.description: Undoes an operation with the same operation (adds to undo addition, multiplies to undo multiplication).
Loses the sign when dividing both sides by a negative coefficient.
Applies an operation to only one side of the equation.

lin_both_sides.description: Moves a term to the other side without changing its sign.
Combines terms that are on opposite sides of the equals sign as if they were on the same side.

lin_general.description: Distributes incorrectly while clearing parentheses in an equation.
Reads 0 = 0 as 'the solution is 0', or a false statement like 0 = 5 as 'x = 5'.

lin_fractions.description: Multiplies only some terms by the LCD when clearing fractions.
Multiplies by a number that does not clear every denominator.

lin_formula.description: Solves for a different variable than the one asked for, or leaves the variable on both sides.
Divides only one term by the coefficient: (y - b)/m written as y - b/m.

lin_ineq.description: Does not reverse the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
Reverses the inequality sign when a negative number is added or subtracted, or when the answer is negative.

app_number.description: Writes an equation that doesn't match the words (a relationship reversed or a quantity left out).
Solves correctly but reports a different quantity than the one asked for.

app_percent.description: Takes the percent of the wrong quantity (the new amount instead of the original).
Uses the percent as a whole number in the equation (30 instead of 0.30).

app_interest.description: Uses the interest rate as a whole number in I = Prt.
Reports the discount (or mark-up) amount as the final price, or the reverse.

app_mixture.description: Mixes up the number of items with their total value (adds values and counts together).
Mixes cents and dollars in the same equation.

app_geometry.description: Adds the legs instead of squaring: c = a + b; or uses a^2 + b^2 with the hypotenuse as a leg.
Uses the area formula for a perimeter problem or the reverse.

app_motion.description: Uses d = r/t or t = d*r instead of d = rt.
Adds distances or rates in a situation where they should be set equal (or the reverse).

app_ineq.description: Uses the wrong inequality direction for 'at least' or 'at most'.
Rounds a boundary the wrong way for a whole-number answer (rounds down when at least is needed).

gr_points.description: Swaps the x- and y-coordinates of an ordered pair.
Substitutes the x-value for y (or the reverse) when checking a solution.

gr_lines.description: Graphs x = a as a horizontal line or y = b as a vertical line.
Computes a point on the line incorrectly while building a table.

gr_intercepts.description: Sets the wrong variable to zero: sets x = 0 to find the x-intercept.
Writes an intercept as the wrong ordered pair, e.g. the x-intercept 3 as (0, 3).

gr_slope.description: Computes run over rise (change in x over change in y).
Subtracts the coordinates in different orders in the numerator and denominator.
Says a vertical line has slope 0 (or a horizontal line has undefined slope).

gr_slope_int.description: Reads the slope from an equation not solved for y (e.g. 2x + 3y = 6 has slope 2).
Uses only the negative (or only the reciprocal) for a perpendicular slope.

gr_line_eq.description: Sign error in point-slope form: y - y1 = m(x - x1) written with + x1 or + y1.
Uses a point's y-coordinate as the y-intercept when the point is not on the y-axis.

gr_ineq2.description: Decides which side is shaded (or whether a point is a solution) by the sign of the inequality alone rather than testing a point.
Treats a strict inequality as including the boundary line (or the reverse).

sys_graph.description: Checks an ordered pair in only one equation of the system.
Thinks lines with the same slope and different intercepts intersect once, or that identical lines have no solution.

sys_substitution.description: Substitutes an expression back into the equation it came from, getting 0 = 0.
Finds one variable and stops, without finding the other.

sys_elimination.description: Multiplies only one side (or only some terms) of an equation before adding.
Adds the equations when the coefficients have the same sign, so nothing cancels, or makes a sign error combining them.

sys_apps.description: Writes only one equation for a problem with two unknowns.
Writes the value equation with counts instead of values (or values instead of counts).

sys_ineq.description: Checks a point in only one of the inequalities.

poly_addsub.description: Subtracting polynomials, changes the sign of only the first term of the second polynomial.
Adds exponents when adding like terms: x^2 + x^2 = x^4.

exp_product.description: Multiplies exponents when multiplying powers of the same base: x^2 * x^3 = x^6.
Adds exponents for a power of a power: (x^2)^3 = x^5.
Raises only the variable, not the coefficient, to a power: (3x)^2 = 3x^2.

poly_mult.description: Multiplies only first and last terms: (x + 3)(x + 2) = x^2 + 6.
Multiplies the monomial by only some terms of the polynomial.

poly_special.description: Squares each term of a binomial: (x + 3)^2 = x^2 + 9.
Keeps a middle term when multiplying conjugates: (x + 3)(x - 3) = x^2 + 6x - 9.

exp_quotient.description: Divides exponents when dividing powers: x^6 / x^2 = x^3.
Evaluates a zero exponent as 0 instead of 1.

poly_divide.description: Divides only the first term of the numerator by the monomial.
In long division, adds instead of subtracting (or subtracts only the first term).

exp_negative.description: Treats a negative exponent as a negative number: x^(-2) = -x^2.
Moves the coefficient along with the variable: 3x^(-2) = 1/(3x^2).

sci_notation.description: Uses the wrong sign for the power of ten (large number with a negative exponent, or the reverse).
Leaves the coefficient outside 1 to 10, e.g. 32 x 10^3.

fac_gcf.description: Factors out a common factor that is not the greatest common factor.
Loses a term (writes nothing instead of 1) after factoring out the GCF: 3x + 3 = 3(x).

fac_trinomial.description: Sign error in a factor, e.g. x^2 - x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2).
Looks for numbers whose sum is c and product is b instead of the reverse.

fac_trinomial_a.description: Factors ax^2 + bx + c as if a were 1.
Does not factor out the GCF first, leaving the factorization incomplete.

fac_special.description: Factors a sum of squares as if it were a difference: x^2 + 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3).
Misremembers the sum/difference of cubes pattern.
Factors a perfect square trinomial ignoring the middle term: x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)(x - 3).

fac_general.description: Stops before factoring completely (a factor that still factors is left).

quad_factor.description: Applies the zero product property when the product equals a nonzero number: (x - 2)(x + 1) = 6 so x = 2 or x = -1.
Divides both sides by x, losing the solution x = 0.
Gives the root of x + 3 = 0 as x = 3.

rat_simplify.description: Cancels opposite factors (a - b)/(b - a) to 1 instead of -1.

rat_muldiv.description: Inverts the first rational expression instead of the second when dividing.
Cancels before factoring numerators and denominators.

rat_add_common.description: Subtracting a numerator with more than one term, changes the sign of only its first term.
Adds the denominators as well as the numerators.

rat_add_unlike.description: Uses a denominator that is not a common multiple of both denominators.
Rewrites a denominator over the LCD without multiplying its numerator by the same factor.

rat_complex.description: Multiplies by the reciprocal of the numerator instead of the denominator.

rat_equations.description: Keeps a solution that makes a denominator zero.
Multiplies only one side (or only some terms) by the LCD.

rat_proportion.description: Multiplies the wrong pairs (numerator by numerator) when cross-multiplying.
Sets up the proportion with non-corresponding sides.

rat_work.description: Adds the times (or averages them) instead of adding the rates 1/a + 1/b = 1/t.

variation.description: Uses y = kx for an inverse variation or y = k/x for a direct one.

rad_sqrt.description: Takes the square root of a sum term by term: sqrt(9 + 16) = 3 + 4.
Halves an odd exponent under a square root, e.g. sqrt(x^5) = x^2.5 left unsimplified, or sqrt(x^6) = x^4.

rad_simplify.description: Removes a square factor that is not the largest, leaving a square factor under the root.
Moves a factor outside the root without taking its square root: sqrt(12) = 4 sqrt(3).

rad_addsub.description: Combines radicals that are only alike after simplifying, without simplifying first (or combines unlike ones).

rad_mult.description: Multiplies coefficients into the radicand: 2 sqrt(3) * sqrt(5) = sqrt(30).
Leaves sqrt(a) * sqrt(a) as sqrt(a^2) or writes it as a^2.

rad_divide.description: Multiplies only the denominator (or only the numerator) by the radical or conjugate.
Multiplies by the same binomial instead of its conjugate.

rad_equations.description: Squares each term of a side separately: (sqrt(x) + 2)^2 = x + 4.
Does not check solutions, keeping an extraneous one.

rad_higher.description: Treats a cube or fourth root like a square root when simplifying.
Says the cube root of a negative number is not a real number.

rat_exponents.description: Reads a^(1/n) as a/n, or a^(m/n) as (a/n)^m.
Swaps the power and the root: a^(2/3) as the square root of a cubed.

quad_sqrt_prop.description: Takes only the positive square root, losing the negative solution.
Takes the square root before isolating the squared term.

quad_complete.description: Adds b^2 instead of (b/2)^2 to complete the square.
Adds the completing term to only one side of the equation.

quad_formula.description: Uses b instead of -b, or divides only the square root by 2a.
Makes a sign error in b^2 - 4ac (e.g. treats (-b)^2 as negative or -4ac with negative c).

quad_apps.description: Keeps a negative (impossible) solution for a length or time.

quad_graph.description: Uses x = b/(2a) instead of x = -b/(2a) for the axis of symmetry.
Gives the axis of symmetry as the vertex, without computing the y-coordinate.
